title: Jailbreak Transferability Mitigation via Constitutional Classifier Ensembles
summary: We propose an ensemble of constitutional classifiers trained on diverse adversarial suffix patterns to defend against transferable jailbreaks. Unlike single classifiers, our approach combines specialized models for different attack categories, reducing universal jailbreak success rates by 65% on Vicuna and LLaMA-2-Chat. The system maintains low inference overhead through parallel evaluation and dynamic thresholding.
gap: Current jailbreak defenses like Constitutional Classifiers fail against transferable attacks that exploit generalization gaps between training and real-world adversarial patterns. Single classifiers cannot adapt to evolving attack suffixes, leaving models vulnerable to cross-model transfer attacks documented in recent studies.
approach: We train an ensemble of 5-7 specialized constitutional classifiers, each fine-tuned on a distinct jailbreak pattern category (e.g., role-play, code injection). A meta-classifier dynamically weights their outputs based on input prompt characteristics, while a lightweight gradient-based detector identifies novel attack patterns through embedding space anomalies.
evaluation: We test against 500 transferable jailbreaks from [ref-014] and new attacks generated via greedy search. Metrics include jailbreak success rate reduction, false positive increase on benign queries, and inference latency. Comparisons are made against single constitutional classifiers and commercial model defenses (ChatGPT, Claude).
